open_items_for_spec_owner.gap: Threshold compares lum(x) >= level - half code (pigment adjust_math THRESHOLD_HALF_CODE, D5 reading PS-C07); at an exact tie the result depends on precision: the CPU reference evaluates in binary64, the GPU kernel in binary32, and on Vulkan (RTX 3090) the tie pixel (7/16, 10/16, 0) lands on the other side of the cut than on DX12 and the CPU
open_items_for_spec_owner.needs: a defined tie rule at the cut (inclusive on the exact rational value, or a stated precision), so cross-backend parity has a target at measure-zero ties
open_items_for_spec_owner.lead_reading: superseded: the boundary-band exemption in render-gpu tests is withdrawn by SMB-R46-FOLLOWUPS-1, which makes the WGSL tie decide as pigment does and restores exact parity
open_items_for_spec_owner.correction: 2026-10-31T05:54:02Z lead correction after R46 F-R46-1: the binary64-vs-binary32 premise was FALSE. pigment Threshold is binary32 end to end (adjust_math.rs:807 apply(rgb: [f32; 3]), :878, blend_math.rs:463 lum -> f32) and kernel.wgsl:361-363 evaluates the same binary32 formula. The tie divergence is Vulkan-specific (pigment white, DX12 white, Vulkan black), most likely contraction (FMA) or evaluation order in the SPIR-V path: UNVERIFIED until the remediation lane measures it. The spec gap that remains is narrower: the Threshold reading should state whether the cut compares the exact rational luminance or round(255 lum) (PS-C07), so every backend has one target.
open_items_for_spec_owner.measured: 2026-10-31T07:34:05Z: SMB-R46-FOLLOWUPS-1 measured the tie: pigment lum and cut 0x3f000000, Vulkan 0x3effffff, DX12 0x3f000000; 49/76 of 1110 tie colours differed per backend, reproduced exactly by FMA contraction in a backend-specific order; the kernel now prevents fusion and both backends match pigment on all 1110; the remaining spec question is only whether the cut is the exact rational or round(255 lum)
